verdict.rationale: Anytype's docs say its own infrastructure handles background syncing and backups automatically [anytype-docs-42], and that content lives in an encrypted Vault that "not even Anytype can see" [anytype-docs-31, anytype-docs-43, anytype-docs-44, anytype-docs-27]. Apps exist for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android [anytype-docs-54], and hands-on users report that cross-device sync "worked great" and describe the protocol as E2E encrypted [anytype-comm-8, anytype-comm-5, anytype-comm-3]. A user notes that data on the local disk is not fully encrypted, and the team says only local indexes are unencrypted; this concerns the device, not what the vendor's sync servers can read, so it does not contradict the claim. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of the encryption and key model behind the vendor-can't-read claim (the pack has only short claims), and full on-device encryption of indexes.
